feedback: If a learner says biodiversity just means lots of animals, define it as the variety of different KINDS of species: 10,000 identical animals is low biodiversity, many different kinds is high.
If a learner says lost species exist elsewhere too, explain that many are endemic — found only in that forest — so losing the forest loses them entirely.

A full response links ~6% of land to >50% of known species, defines biodiversity as variety, and justifies the conservation priority; a partial response knows rainforests are rich but can't yet articulate the disproportion or the variety definition.
activities.intendedInsight: Biodiversity means the VARIETY of different species, not just the number of animals; many tropical rainforest species are endemic (found nowhere else), so clearing their only habitat can wipe those species out entirely — this is why protection is a priority.
learnerActions: Answer the diagnostic prompt: 'Rainforests cover only about 6% of Earth's land. If they're such a small slice of the planet, why do scientists say protecting them matters so much for life on Earth? Tell me why, and then tell me what biodiversity actually means here.'
Decide whether 10,000 animals that are all the same species would count as high biodiversity, and justify your answer.
Explain why we can't simply recreate a cleared rainforest's species somewhere else.
Write a short justification linking the 6%-of-land to the >50%-of-species figure and using it to argue for conservation priority.
activities.title: What 'biodiversity' really means, and why loss is irreversible
